context_sources.operation: empty() (210-217): a default-constructed test over id_, hits_, the significance threshold, the score type and higher_score_better -- NOT an empty-hit-list test, which is why FileInfo.cpp:1347 does not guard the read at :1352

getNTerminalModificationName (1671-1676) and getCTerminalModificationName (1688-1693): both return ResidueModification::getId(), while the residue modifications at FileInfo.cpp:1366 are counted by getFullId()
the user-defined (mass-only) modifications at 593, 631 and 671 set FullId but not Id, so getId() is empty for them and the modification count uses the empty key
updateRanges(): every consensus feature's own position and intensity, then each of its sub-features', interleaved
IndexLess (155-165): the HandleSetType order is (map_index, unique_id), which is the order the -s element loops accumulate in
percentOf (280-290) and roundTo (245-261): the FASTA percentages, with a zero total answering 0.0
SummaryStatistics (933-963): sorts in place, zeroes every field for an empty sample and substitutes 0.0 for the variance of one value; mean (102-120) accumulates into a double
the global operator+(std::string, double) at 859-920: the modified-top-hit percentage is rendered by appendToStr, not by the report stream's precision

upstream_test_definition.comparison: the reports are compared byte for byte with the Release C++ output the oracle retained, after replacing the two lines that embed the input path

method: Library-level: FileInfo::run on each input with the flags the oracle passed the tool; text and TSV compared byte for byte with the retained Release C++ reports after replacing the 'File name: ' text line and the 'general: file name' TSV line, which embed the input path. The FASTA duplicate warnings, which the source writes with OPENMS_LOG_WARN rather than into the reports, are compared with the tool's stderr.
evidence: Tier 1 (executed differential): the Release C++ FileInfo of openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576, at all three pins this port follows, ran 63 cases on ibminode06 twice, reproduced (../oracle/a7-fileinfo/manifest.json). 43 of them have both reports compared here byte for byte, two of them (c_zero_intensity_s and c_zero_intensity_all) with the single documented exception of the NaN spelling on exactly one line, which the test asserts rather than masks; the rest carry refusals, exit codes and the duplicate warnings. One mask only: the "FileInfo took" stdout line, which goes into neither -out nor -out_tsv. Tier 1 (retained upstream definition): TOPP_FileInfo_7, _10, _13, _17, _18 and _20 reproduced with their own flags; _14 and _15 pass -v, which is not ported, so their inputs run without it. Tier 1 (executed probe): scripts/probe_std_hash.cpp pins libstdc++'s std::hash<std::string> over the empty string, every tail length, bytes above 0x7f and an embedded NUL, and 28 of its 60 values are asserted in a unit test of src/format/file_info/fasta.rs. Tier 4: the three out-of-bounds std::vector accesses are refused under decision D1, and the ValidationInfo, CorruptionInfo and DetailInfo aggregates these branches never fill stay at their defaults.

known_gaps.what: a consensus sub-feature whose map index is at or beyond the column-header count is refused, where the C++ reports
known_gaps.why: FileInfo.cpp:1175-1183 sizes one occurrence vector from getColumnHeaders().size() and then indexes it with FeatureHandle::getMapIndex(), which is the file's map= id and not a position. Measured on the Release build: a7_cons_no_headers.consensusXML segmentation-faults; a7_cons_mapindex_high.consensusXML, a7_cons_ids_one_based.consensusXML and the UPSTREAM ConsensusID_3_input.consensusXML exit 0 and print a WRONG peptide row (ConsensusID_3's two maps are numbered 1 and 2, and the report says its peptides were `observed in 1 maps` when they are in both). Decision D1 refuses an out-of-bounds access, so the port returns Error::InvalidValue before writing anything.
known_gaps.owner: this package (documented native difference); the source defect is recorded for OpenMS_CPP_ISSUES.md

known_gaps.what: an identification file with no protein identification run is refused
known_gaps.why: FileInfo.cpp:1336-1341 reads id_data.proteins[0] unconditionally, while the structured block at :1451 guards the same access with if (!id_data.proteins.empty()). Measured on the Release build: a7_id_no_runs.idXML segmentation-faults. This crate refuses the file one layer earlier: the idXML reader itself rejects it with 'idXML needs at least one IdentificationRun' (src/format/idxml.rs:310) and the tool exits 3, not the 6 the branch's own guard would give; mzidentml.rs:1596-1598 rejects a document with no SpectrumIdentification element just as early. The branch's proteins.first() guard therefore has no reachable input and stays as a defence.
known_gaps.owner: this package (documented native difference); the source defect is recorded for OpenMS_CPP_ISSUES.md

known_gaps.what: a peptide identification with no hit is refused
known_gaps.why: FileInfo.cpp:1354 reads temp_hits[0] behind the guard !id_data.peptides[i].empty(), but PeptideIdentification::empty() (PeptideIdentification.cpp:210-217) tests for a default-constructed object and also checks id_, which IdXMLFile::load always fills from the enclosing IdentificationRun. The guard therefore never protects the read for a LOADED file. Measured on the Release build: a7_id_empty_hitlist.idXML and a7_id_empty_hitlist_ok.idXML, the second with an empty score type, both segmentation-fault.
known_gaps.owner: this package (documented native difference); the source defect is recorded for OpenMS_CPP_ISSUES.md

known_gaps.what: a FASTA sequence holding a byte outside ASCII is refused
known_gaps.why: the source counts and prints raw chars, so such a byte reaches the report as that single byte; this port's reports are Rust strings and the FASTA reader only yields such a byte as part of a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence, so no faithful rendering exists. src/format/file_info/fasta.rs::reject_non_ascii refuses before anything is written. No upstream fixture contains one.

known_gaps.what: an idXML with more than 14 modified peptide hits cannot be loaded, so two oracle cases have no differential
known_gaps.why: AASequence::parse_with_budget (src/chemistry/sequence.rs:1147-1180) charges a per-modified-sequence preflight proportional to ModificationsDB::len() against the single document-wide XmlLimits::max_work = 50_000_000 (src/format/identification_xml.rs:411-425). Measured: 14 modified hits load, 15 do not, while 800 unmodified hits are fine. FileFilter_25_input.idXML (473 modified hits) and FalseDiscoveryRate_5_input.idXML (75) are therefore refused with "peptide parent parsing resource limit exceeded"; the oracle records what the C++ prints for both.
known_gaps.owner: the shared identification-XML reader and AASequence parsing budget, not this package

known_gaps.what: the consensusXML -s `qualities` block summarises twice as many values as there are consensus features
known_gaps.why: FileInfo.cpp:2263-2266 declares vector<double> qualities(size) -- size zero-initialised values -- and then appends to it, so the sample is 2*size long with size leading zeros. `widths` has the same defect and is never printed. This is reproduced, not refused: it is deterministic, in bounds and recorded in the UPSTREAM expected output FileInfo_7_output.txt (five consensus features, `num. of values: 10` for the qualities). The source defect is recorded for OpenMS_CPP_ISSUES.md.

known_gaps.what: a NaN variance is written `nan` where the reference build writes `-nan`
known_gaps.why: FileInfo.cpp:2310 divides each sub-feature's intensity by the centroid's and :2312-2315 inverts every ratio below 1, so a sub-feature of intensity 0 under a positive centroid contributes 1/0 = +inf; Math::SummaryStatistics (StatisticFunctions.h:933-958) then has mean = +inf and Math::variance (:541-556) adds (1-inf)^2 = +inf to (inf-inf)^2 = NaN. In bounds and reproducible in both oracle runs, so D1 reproduces it. The VALUE is reproduced exactly: measured on x86_64, inf - inf is 0xfff8000000000000 (SSE2's default NaN, sign bit set) in the reference build and in this crate's variance_with_mean alike, both probes fed from argv so nothing is constant-folded. Only the spelling differs: glibc writes a negative NaN as -nan, while src/format/file_info/text_format.rs writes every NaN as nan by design, because the sign of a GENERATED NaN belongs to the hardware (AArch64's default NaN is positive, and this crate's CI runs the full suite on macos-latest) and Apple libc writes nan for 0xfff8000000000000 anyway -- ../oracle/file-info-text-format measured that exact bit pattern and tests/file_info_text_format.rs asserts the nan it produced. Oracle cases c_zero_intensity, c_zero_intensity_s and c_zero_intensity_all on a7_cons_zero_intensity.consensusXML; consensus_zero_intensity_sub_feature_makes_the_variance_a_nan asserts that exactly one line of the frozen Release report differs and that it differs in exactly this way.
known_gaps.owner: the FileInfo text layer (src/format/file_info/text_format.rs, package A2); this package pins the one report that reaches it

known_gaps.what: -m, -p and -s on an mzIdentML input report an empty MSExperiment
known_gaps.why: none of the three sections has an MZIDENTML arm, so all three fall into the trailing `else //peaks` arm (FileInfo.cpp:2005, :2115, :2384) and report the experiment the identification branch never loaded. Reproduced verbatim, including the empty document id and the 0000-00-00 00:00:00 date; oracle cases mzid14_all and mzid15_all.
